title: Cold rebuild: the multipart planner
summary: Rebuild the multipart upload planner from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove it stuck. You built **a multipart upload planner** in *Object storage: blobs out of the
database*. Now write it again from an **empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The
tests are exactly the ones you passed the first time.
Why: the limits (5 MiB to 5 GiB parts, 10,000 parts, 5 TiB objects) come up whenever someone's large upload
fails at 50 GB. Reading your old code feels like knowing it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: A client uploads a 200 GiB file with 8 MiB parts and the store rejects the upload. Why?
options: 200 GiB / 8 MiB is 25,600 parts, over the 10,000-part limit: use parts of at least 21 MiB
Parts must be at least 64 MiB
Objects over 5 GiB cannot be stored
The last part must be exactly 8 MiB
steps.explain: 200 GiB is 204,800 MiB; divided into 10,000 parts that is 20.48 MiB, so 21 MiB parts fit. Single PUTs stop at 5 GiB, but multipart objects go up to 5 TiB.

steps.prompt: Ten consumers read a topic with four partitions in one consumer group. How many consume?
options: It depends on the message keys
steps.explain: Each partition is assigned to at most one member of a group, so six members sit idle until partitions are added or members leave.

steps.title: Cold rebuild: PlanParts
prompt: Write `long[] PlanParts(long size, long preferredPart)`, from memory:
- the part size starts at `preferredPart`, clamped to 5 MiB .. 5 GiB;
- if that needs more than 10,000 parts, use the smallest whole number of MiB that fits in 10,000 parts;
- every part has that size except the last, which holds the rest.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
